name: KATE (KNN-Augmented in-conTExt Example selection) - What Makes Good In-Context Examples for GPT-3?
venue: DeeLIO@ACL 2022 (Workshop on Knowledge Extraction and Integration for Deep Learning Architectures); first released as arXiv:2101.06804 (Jan 2021). ACL Anthology 2022.deelio-1.10, DOI 10.18653/v1/2022.deelio-1.10.
authors_affiliation: Jiachang Liu (Duke University; intern at Microsoft), Dinghan Shen (Microsoft), Yizhe Zhang (Microsoft), Bill Dolan (Microsoft), Lawrence Carin (Duke University), Weizhu Chen (Microsoft). Work done while Jiachang Liu (intern) and Yizhe Zhang were at Microsoft.
task_domain: NLP in-context learning: sentiment analysis (text classification), table-to-text generation, and open-domain question answering (QA). Demonstration/example selection for few-shot prompting of GPT-3.
problem_setting: Offline, single-model (GPT-3 via API, no fine-tuning), single-turn in-context few-shot learning. A labeled training set is available from which in-context examples are selected; GPT-3's parameters are frozen and inaccessible. The work addresses the sensitivity of GPT-3's few-shot performance to the choice of in-context examples and asks whether selecting semantically similar examples (vs random sampling) improves results. Single-agent, non-interactive prompt construction; the GPT-3 API is called once per test query with temperature 0.
what_is_retrieved: In-context demonstrations (labeled training examples / demos, i.e. (x, y) input-output pairs) to be placed in the GPT-3 prompt.
retrieval_grounding: STATIC external corpus: retrieval is over the fixed labeled training set of the target task (and, for QA, the question-answer training pairs). No growing/episodic memory written by the model.
completeness_vs_topk_objective: Fixed top-k ranking: for each test query, retrieve the k nearest-neighbor training examples by embedding similarity, where k is a preset hyperparameter (3 for sentiment, 2 for ToTTo due to token limit, 64 for NQ/WQ, 10 for TriviaQA). Not a completeness-recovery or variable-size precision objective.
cbr_cycle_coverage: Retrieve (yes) / Reuse (yes, verbatim as ICL exemplars) / Revise (no) / Retain (no) — only Retrieve and Reuse are implemented.
explicit_cbr_grounding: False: the work does not frame itself as case-based reasoning and does not cite Aamodt & Plaza / Kolodner. It is framed as retrieval-augmented in-context example selection (kNN over sentence embeddings); it does reference retrieve-and-edit literature (Hashimoto et al. 2018) and kNN-LM/kNN-MT.
retrieval_unit: Single demonstration (one training (source, target) example / (x_i, y_i) pair); the query key is the source sentence x_i embedding. For QA, a retrieved unit is a question-answer pair.
index_source: Static, offline corpus = the target task's training set. Sentence embeddings of all training sources are precomputed offline; the test source is encoded on the fly. No online/test-time induction of new store entries.
index_structure_topology: Flat vector index over sentence-embedding vectors of training sources; nearest neighbors found by Euclidean distance (for KATE_roberta) or cosine similarity (for KATE_nli / KATE_nli+sts-b). No graph or hierarchy.
retriever_type: Dense retriever: off-the-shelf pretrained/fine-tuned sentence encoders (RoBERTa-large CLS embeddings; Sentence-BERT-style encoders fine-tuned on NLI / STS-B / SST-2) used for kNN search. No BM25, no LLM-as-retriever.
retriever_learning_signal: None for the core method (off-the-shelf encoders, no retriever training against downstream task). The retriever is a frozen pretrained sentence encoder. The paper additionally studies encoders that were independently fine-tuned (with contrastive/similarity objectives) on auxiliary datasets (NLI, STS-B, SST-2), showing task-related fine-tuning of the encoder helps, but this fine-tuning is not driven by GPT-3 / LM-feedback or downstream-task reward — it is supervised similarity training on external datasets.
query_construction: Raw test input (test source sentence x_test) is encoded directly by the sentence encoder; no decomposition, expansion, or thought-conditioning. The embedding of the raw query is used for nearest-neighbor search.
query_granularity: Task-level / one-shot at t=0: a single retrieval is performed per test instance before the single GPT-3 call. No step-level or trajectory-level retrieval.
when_to_retrieve: One-shot: retrieval happens once per test query to build the prompt, then GPT-3 is called a single time. No iterative or uncertainty-triggered retrieval.
retrieval_trigger_signal: Fixed schedule: retrieval is always performed once per test example before prompt construction; there is no confidence-, attention-, or classifier-based trigger.
reranking: No dedicated reranking stage. Retrieved neighbors are ordered by similarity score; the only ordering study is whether default vs reverse vs random permutation of the selected k examples in the prompt matters (found to have small effect, data-dependent).
retrieved_context_refinement: None (beyond similarity ordering). No decomposition, distillation, distractor filtering, or compression of retrieved examples; a minor ToTTo-specific preprocessing deletes closing angle brackets to fit the 2048-token limit, but this is input formatting, not refinement of retrieved content.
index_content_separation: N/A: examples are short text pairs; no separation of a lightweight index from heavy on-demand content.
how_retrieved_used: Prompt augmentation: the k retrieved (x_i, y_i) demonstrations are concatenated, ordered by similarity, to form the context C, then C is prepended to the test source x_test and fed to GPT-3 ([C; x_test]) to generate the answer. Verbatim in-context exemplars; no adaptation, no training signal.
planning_integration: N/A for planning/acting in the agentic sense. KATE provides one-shot exemplars at prompt-construction time for a single forward generation; there is no planner, no per-step interleaving, no tree search.
reasoning_search_interleaving_granularit: Per-answer: retrieval occurs once and the entire answer is generated in a single GPT-3 call; retrieval is not interleaved with reasoning steps, sentences, or tool calls.
adaptation_mechanism: Verbatim ICL exemplar: retrieved training examples are inserted unchanged into the prompt; no LLM-prompted adaptation, execution-feedback revision, or critic-guided revision.
retrieved_item_representation: Raw demonstration text: the surface (source, target) pairs of retrieved training examples inserted verbatim into the prompt (e.g. table-to-text pairs, question-answer pairs, sentence-label pairs). No distillation, workflow, program, or latent token form.
abstraction_level_of_retrieved_unit: Single raw demonstration (concrete labeled training instance); no distilled strategy, guideline, workflow, or skill abstraction.
noise_robustness_mechanism: None explicit. The implicit robustness mechanism is semantic-similarity selection itself (closer examples give better results, shown via closest-vs-farthest study). No relevance evaluator, self-reflection, retriever-aware training, or distractor-aware SFT.
memory_type: none (static training set used as a fixed example pool; no episodic/skill/workflow/procedural/graph/latent memory).
write_back: False: the system never writes new experiences/cases/skills back into any store; the training set is fixed and read-only.
online_growth: False: the retrievable store (training set) does not grow during deployment/test time; it is frozen offline.
failure_experience_usage: None: only the labeled training examples (treated as positive demonstrations) are used; no storage or contrastive use of failed/negative experiences. A separate kNN-only baseline (predict via neighbor labels / majority voting) is studied but it is a baseline, not a memory mechanism.
memory_evolution_update: N/A / none: no stored entries are mutated (store is static, append-only is not even used).
retrieval_as_learned_policy: No: retrieval is a fixed similarity top-k (nearest neighbors by Euclidean/cosine distance in a frozen embedding space), not a learned/RL-optimized selection policy.
cross_agent_or_cross_framework_sharing: No: single-model, single-agent prompting; no cross-agent or cross-framework memory sharing.
benchmarks: SST-2 (train) -> IMDB (test) for sentiment analysis; ToTTo (table-to-text generation, dev set, incl. overlap and nonoverlap subsets); Natural Questions (NQ), WebQuestions (WQ), and TriviaQA for open-domain QA. Backbone LLM: GPT-3 (via OpenAI API, temperature 0). Sentence encoders: RoBERTa-large, and RoBERTa-large fine-tuned on SNLI+MultiNLI (nli), then STS-B (nli+sts-b), and SST-2.
benchmark_family: QA (open-domain: NQ, WQ, TriviaQA), text classification / sentiment (SST-2 -> IMDB), and table-to-text generation (ToTTo). Not in the agentic/web/embodied/tool/code/memory families.
baselines: Random (random sampling of in-context examples from the training set, averaged over 5 trials with std); kNN_roberta (non-parametric kNN classifier/predictor using retrieved neighbors' targets via top-1 or majority voting, same RoBERTa-large embedding space, no GPT-3); GPT-3 (64 examples) figures from Brown et al. 2020; and fine-tuned reference systems for context: T5 (fine-tuned, 11B / closed-book T5, T5+SSM), and RAG (open-domain) for QA.
key_metrics: Accuracy (sentiment/IMDB); BLEU and PARENT (ToTTo, overall/overlap/nonoverlap); Exact Match (EM) score (NQ, WQ, TriviaQA).
headline_result: KATE consistently beats random selection. Reported abstract headlines (published v2): table-to-text generation 44.3% on ToTTo and open-domain QA 45.5% on NQ (the abstract's NQ figure is stated as a relative/best-setting gain; in Table 6 KATE_nli+sts-b reaches EM 41.6 on NQ test vs Random 28.6, and on WQ KATE_nli reaches 50.6 vs Random 41.0). On IMDB, KATE_sst-2 = 93.43% accuracy vs Random 87.95% (vs fine-tuned T5 95.2%). On ToTTo dev, KATE_roberta = 41.0 BLEU / 50.6 PARENT vs Random 28.4 / 39.3 (vs fine-tuned T5 41.2 / 53.0). Note: arXiv v1 abstract cites 41.9% on ToTTo; the published version cites 44.3% on ToTTo.
ablations: (1) Closest vs farthest neighbors on NQ subset of 100 (EM 46.0 closest vs 31.0 farthest) — motivates similarity-based selection. (2) kNN_roberta baseline (no GPT-3) performs near random guessing / much worse, showing the retrieval module is complementary to GPT-3, not sufficient alone. (3) Choice of sentence encoder: encoders fine-tuned on task-similar data help (KATE_sst-2 best on IMDB; KATE_nli / KATE_nli+sts-b best on QA), while fine-tuning on a dissimilar objective (NLI/STS-B for IMDB/ToTTo) slightly hurts. (4) Number of in-context examples (5/10/20/35/64 on NQ): both KATE and random improve with more examples, but KATE dominates even with as few as 5. (5) Training-set size (retrieval pool size): larger pool improves KATE EM but barely changes random. (6) Order of in-context examples (default / reverse / 3 random permutations on NQ): small effect, data-dependent (reverse best on NQ; default slightly better on WQ/TriviaQA).
evaluation_decoupling: No: only end-to-end task metrics (Accuracy, BLEU/PARENT, EM) are reported; no separate intrinsic retrieval metrics such as Recall@k or nDCG. The closest-vs-farthest study is reported via downstream EM, not retrieval IR metrics.
process_vs_outcome_metrics: Outcome only: evaluation scores final task output (answer correctness, generation quality). Qualitative case studies of retrieved examples are shown but no quantitative intermediate/process metrics.
cost_efficiency_tradeoff: KATE calls the GPT-3 API only once per test query (contrasted with contextual calibration which repeats per token), framed as inference-efficient. Using fewer in-context examples (e.g. 5) still beats random, enabling cheaper/shorter prompts. ToTTo uses only 2 examples due to the GPT-3 2048-token limit. No detailed latency/dollar-cost numbers reported.
context_budget_and_selection_count: Fixed-k per task, budget-capped by GPT-3's 2048-token input limit: k=3 for sentiment (more did not help), k=2 for ToTTo (token-limit constrained), k=64 for NQ/WQ, k=10 for TriviaQA (64 retrieved examples would exceed the token limit). Selected examples are ordered by similarity.
benchmark_construction_and_size: N/A (not a benchmark paper; uses existing datasets SST-2/IMDB, ToTTo, NQ, WQ, TriviaQA).
builds_on: GPT-3 in-context learning (Brown et al. 2020); retrieve-and-edit / retrieval-augmented generation literature (Hashimoto et al. 2018); kNN-augmented LM/MT methods (kNN-LM Khandelwal et al. 2019, kNN-MT Khandelwal et al. 2020, BERT-kNN Kassner & Schutze 2020); Sentence-BERT (Reimers & Gurevych 2019) and RoBERTa (Liu et al. 2019) sentence encoders.
contrasts_with: Random sampling of in-context examples (the GPT-3 default in Brown et al. 2020); contextual calibration (Zhao et al. 2021, which must repeat per generated token); prompt-based fine-tuning of smaller LMs LM-BFF (Gao et al. 2020) and AutoPrompt (Shin et al. 2020); fine-tuned models T5 / T5+SSM and RAG (used as reference upper bounds); the kNN-only non-parametric baseline (kNN modifies the prediction whereas KATE modifies the conditional context).
lineage: Group A (ICL demonstration retrieval). KATE is the founding similarity-based / kNN demonstration retriever for in-context learning: it established the dense-embedding nearest-neighbor demo-selection paradigm that later learned/retriever-trained demo selectors (e.g. EPR, learning-to-retrieve-prompts) build upon and contrast against.
